gold_standard: repoDB (Brown & Patel, Sci Data 2017) — Approved vs failed (Terminated/Withdrawn/Suspended)
scoring: Mechanism-only (target + direction-aware pathway + PPI); clinical/literature/regulatory features removed to prevent retrospective leakage.

disease_genes_genetics_weighted.note: Genetics-weighted = disease genes weighted by Open Targets genetic_association score (Nelson 2015); also reduces leakage vs the overall OT score (no known-drug channel).

findings.title: Retrospective repurposing recovery (mechanism-only) vs repoDB
findings.detail: On 1,476 repoDB drug-indication pairs across 55 diseases, the engine's leakage-free mechanistic score separates Approved from failed repurposings with AUROC 0.7347 (AUPRC 0.8198, BEDROC 0.8472, EF@10% 1.28x), vs random 0.4939 and target-only 0.7464.
findings.capa: Re-run on each data refresh; track AUROC over time. Below 0.55 triggers review of the biology inputs (Open Targets gene sets, mechanism coverage).

findings.title: Ablation: does the direction-aware pathway term help?
findings.detail: AUROC with direction-aware pathway scoring 0.7347 vs direction-blind 0.735 (delta -0.0003); pathway excluded 0.7438.
findings.capa: If delta is consistently <=0, revert the pathway term to direction-blind.

findings.title: Negative control
findings.detail: Shuffling the labels collapses AUROC to 0.4794 (expected ~0.5), confirming the signal is not an artefact of the evaluation.

findings.title: Genetics-weighted disease genes — tested, neutral
findings.detail: Weighting disease genes by Open Targets genetic_association (Nelson 2015) gives AUROC 0.7297 vs flat 0.7347 (lift -0.005) — neutral on retrospective recovery. The tiny flat-over-genetics gap also confirms the headline score is NOT meaningfully inflated by the overall-score known-drug channel. Genetics enrichment is now fetched per disease and available as an opt-in, leakage-safer target weighting; it is NOT the engine default (no measured benefit).
findings.capa: Keep genetics weighting opt-in; revisit for prospective validation where the Nelson prior is more relevant than retrospective overlap.

findings.title: KG-embedding ensemble fails the EXTERNAL benchmark — not integrated
findings.detail: On 443 KG-mappable repoDB pairs, the KG embedding alone scores AUROC 0.5358 (~chance) and the mechanistic+KG ensemble 0.7007 vs mechanistic 0.7553 (lift -0.0546). The +0.042 seen on Hetionet's own held-out treats did NOT transfer to discriminating real-world approved-vs-failed repurposings.
findings.capa: Do NOT wire the KG embedding into the engine — it degrades the mechanistic score on the external benchmark. Revisit only with metapath/DWPC features or a better-generalising model.
